question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=2 \sin{\left(x \right)}$ and $v=x.$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}&=2 \cos{\left(x \right)}\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=\frac{v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}-u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}}{v^{2}}\\ &=\frac{(x)\cdot (2 \cos{\left(x \right)})-(2 \sin{\left(x \right)})\cdot (1)}{(x)^{2}}\\ &=\frac{2 x \cos{\left(x \right)} - 2 \sin{\left(x \right)}}{x^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
